title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics

epigraph.quote: In continuous-process chemicals, your gross margin is decided by feedstock logistics and tail-gas recovery long before your sales team quotes a price.
epigraph.author: Process Manufacturing Economics

web_blocks.html: PCBL's supply chain is built around two physical facts of carbon black. First, it is bulky to ship long distances relative to its value. Second, its main input—Carbon Black Feedstock (CBFS), a heavy oil from refining and coal tar—makes up 65%–70% of operating costs. So PCBL placed its main Indian plants near deep-water ports and tire hubs. Mundra and Palej in Gujarat serve western auto hubs and Arabian Sea shipping lanes. Kochi sits near southern rubber belts and port berths, while Durgapur serves eastern industry. The automated Tamil Nadu complex sits right in the Chennai auto belt (Apollo, MRF, Michelin, JK Tyre) with easy coastal export access.

Western tire and coatings buyers demand just-in-time delivery rather than 45-day sea transit. To serve them, PCBL built warehouses in Antwerp, Belgium, and leased railcar fleets in the United States. Aquapharm's supply chain relies on yellow phosphorus, phosphorus trichloride (PCl3), and specialty amines across Mahad and Pirangut (India), Texas (USA), and Jeddah (Saudi Arabia). Local plants in Texas and Jeddah shield part of Aquapharm's US and Middle East volume from ocean freight spikes. However, Indian exports to the US and Europe still face container rate and tariff swings.

web_blocks.caption: PCBL Chemical Consolidated FY26 (Mar 2026) Revenue-to-Cash Waterfall (₹ Crore; Screener consolidated Expenses of ₹7,146 Cr combine feedstock, employee, and plant operating costs)
web_blocks.takeaway: Out of ₹8,189 Cr FY26 revenue, operating expenses consumed ₹7,146 Cr (87.3%), leaving ₹1,043 Cr EBITDA (12.7%). Fixed charges—₹373 Cr D&A plus ₹423 Cr interest—absorbed 76.3% of EBITDA, leaving just ₹198 Cr net profit (2.4% PAT margin). Yet working-capital release drove ₹1,576 Cr CFO and ₹851 Cr FCF.

web_blocks.html: The FY26 unit-economics waterfall shows the core tension in PCBL's P&L. At the plant level, conversion economics stayed solid: every ₹100 of sales produced ₹12.74 of EBITDA in FY26. Working capital release lifted operating cash flow to ₹19.25 per ₹100 of sales (₹1,576 crore). Below EBITDA, however, post-Aquapharm debt and depreciation took a heavy toll. Depreciation (₹373 crore, or 4.55% of sales) and interest (₹423 crore, or 5.17% of sales) consumed ₹796 crore—over three-quarters of operating profit. That squeezed pre-tax margin to 3.19% (₹261 crore) and net margin to just 2.42% (₹198 crore).

web_blocks.takeaway: Core carbon black unit economics rebounded strongly in H1 FY27 after management sacrificed low-margin spot exports, whereas Aquapharm's EBITDA margin remains stuck near 10%—roughly half its pre-acquisition level.

web_blocks.html: A key trait of carbon black economics is the gap between formula contracts and spot timing. About 70%–75% of domestic rubber black sells on quarterly formula contracts that pass through CBFS moves with a one-quarter lag. When crude and CBFS drop fast—as in parts of FY26—two pressures hit at once. First, PCBL takes inventory losses on higher-cost CBFS in its tanks; second, spot rivals running cheaper fresh oil undercut export prices, pulling blended EBITDA/t toward ₹13,500/t. When management holds price discipline—as in Q2 FY27, when it cut low-margin exports 18% QoQ—underlying EBITDA/t snaps back to ₹17,500/t (and ₹19,800/t with a ₹2,300/t US tariff refund).

Working capital is the other quiet driver of unit economics. When crude falls, lower input prices shrink the rupee value of receivables and inventory, freeing cash. Between FY25 and FY26, PCBL cut debtor days from 78 to 62 and inventory days from 80 to 65 while holding payable days near 92. That cut the Cash Conversion Cycle from 57 days to 35 days and pushed Working Capital Days to -40 days. It explains why FY26 generated ₹1,576 crore of operating cash flow even as net profit fell 54.5%. Investors must note that this cash tailwind reverses when crude oil prices rally.

web_blocks.title: Read EBITDA per Tonne Ex-One-Offs and Normalize Working Capital
paragraphs: Do not treat one quarter's headline EBITDA/t or 158% CFO/EBITDA conversion as a steady state. In Q2 FY27, ₹2,300/t of the ₹19,800/t reported EBITDA/t came from a one-off US tariff refund.
Likewise, ₹851 Cr of FY26 Free Cash Flow got a boost from falling input prices freeing working capital. When crude rises, inventory absorption will pull CFO/EBITDA back toward 70%–85%.

web_blocks.html: Co-generated green power is the quiet stabilizer inside PCBL's conversion-cost structure. Every tonne of carbon black manufactured in a furnace reactor yields high-calorific tail gas; rather than flaring it, PCBL routes that gas into captive steam turbines totaling ~122 MW across Durgapur (30 MW), Palej (12 MW), Kochi, Mundra, and Tamil Nadu. This self-generated electricity covers plant parasitic loads—primarily high-pressure air blowers, pelletizers, and bag-house filtration—and exports surplus megawatts to state grids. Because tail-gas power carries near-zero marginal fuel cost once the reactor is running, it acts as a structural ₹1,500–₹2,000 per tonne cost buffer relative to unintegrated smaller producers.

book_paragraphs: If you want to understand why PCBL can generate ₹1,576 crore of operating cash flow in the exact same year its net profit falls 54.5%, you have to look under the hood at its unit economics. Carbon black is a deceptively physical business. You start with Carbon Black Feedstock—heavy aromatic oil left over from crude refining or coal-tar distillation—which makes up roughly two-thirds of your cost of goods. You crack it at extreme temperatures inside refractory-lined reactors, collect the fine black powder, pelletize it, and use the hot waste tail gas to spin turbines that generate 122 MW of electricity. That co-generated power runs your own compressors and bag filters and sells surplus electricity back to the grid, giving a scaled player like PCBL a built-in cost advantage over smaller, unintegrated plants.

Logistics matter just as much as reactors. Carbon black is dusty, low-density, and expensive to haul across continents, so PCBL placed its plants right next to ports and tire hubs: Mundra and Palej on the west coast, Kochi in the southwest, Durgapur in the east, and its automated Tamil Nadu facility right in the heart of India's southern automotive corridor. To win export business in Europe and North America, PCBL also set up warehouses in Antwerp and railcar distribution in the US, because an OEM tire plant will not wait six weeks for a container ship when it runs just-in-time inventory.

Now let us walk through every ₹100 of revenue PCBL earned in FY26, because that single-year waterfall tells the entire financial story. Out of ₹8,189 crore in consolidated sales, operating expenses—mostly feedstock, plant conversion, and staff—took ₹7,146 crore, or ₹87.26 out of every ₹100. That left ₹1,043 crore of operating EBITDA, or ₹12.74 per ₹100 of sales. In a low-debt business, 12.7% EBITDA in a downcycle would be perfectly respectable. But here is where the Aquapharm debt bites: depreciation took ₹373 crore (₹4.55 per ₹100) and interest expense took ₹423 crore (₹5.17 per ₹100). Together, those two fixed charges ate 76.3% of operating profit! After ₹14 crore of other income and ₹63 crore of taxes, only ₹198 crore—barely ₹2.42 out of every ₹100 of sales—made it down to net profit.

Why, then, did cash flow look so strong? Because when crude oil and feedstock prices soften, your working capital shrinks automatically. In FY26, PCBL trimmed debtor days from 78 to 62 and inventory days from 80 to 65 while keeping supplier payables at 92 days. That pulled the Cash Conversion Cycle down from 57 days to 35 days and released hundreds of crores of cash, lifting operating cash flow to ₹1,576 crore and free cash flow to ₹851 crore. Just remember the flip side: when crude oil rallies, that working-capital engine runs in reverse and absorbs cash.

On a per-tonne basis, FY26 and H1 FY27 also taught us a valuable lesson about pricing discipline. During Q4 FY26, when Chinese and Russian spot surpluses flooded export markets, PCBL's carbon black EBITDA per tonne sank to roughly ₹13,516. Rather than chasing empty tonnage, management deliberately walked away from 18% of its lower-margin export volume in Q2 FY27, dropping quarterly sales to 134,180 tonnes. The payoff was immediate: underlying carbon black EBITDA per tonne rebounded to ₹17,500—or ₹19,800 including a one-time ₹2,300/t US tariff refund. Meanwhile, Aquapharm is still searching for its footing, posting ₹433 crore revenue and ₹42 crore EBITDA in Q2 FY27—a 9.7% margin that remains roughly half of what it earned before PCBL bought it.

Follow the working-capital conveyor belt from ship to furnace to customer invoice. Because PCBL imports carbon black feedstock (CBFS) and ethylene cracker bottoms in bulk parcels, a sixty-to-ninety-day raw-material pipeline sits between crude oil price moves and finished-goods dispatch.

In standard rubber grades, formula-linked contracts pass through feedstock swings with a one-quarter lag, which protects long-term rupee spreads per tonne even though reported revenue fluctuates wildly with crude oil. That is why you and I never judge a carbon black producer by percentage EBITDA margin alone; we always track EBITDA per metric tonne.

In FY26, PCBL's finance team deserves genuine credit for tightening the cash conversion cycle from 57 days to 35 days—freeing ₹1,576 Cr of operating cash flow and ₹851 Cr of free cash flow despite softer consolidated profitability. That cash engine is the single biggest buffer protecting the balance sheet while Aquapharm's margins remain depressed.

book_subsections.title: The Working-Capital Accordion: Why Falling Crude Releases Cash and Rising Crude Absorbs It
paragraphs: One of the most common mistakes investors make in feedstock-intensive chemical businesses is misreading a single year's cash conversion. In FY25, PCBL earned ₹1,337 crore of operating profit, yet Cash Flow from Operations was only ₹760 crore (70% pre-tax CFO/EBITDA) and Free Cash Flow was -₹4 crore. One year later, in FY26, operating profit fell 22% to ₹1,043 crore, yet Cash Flow from Operations more than doubled to ₹1,576 crore (158% pre-tax CFO/EBITDA) and Free Cash Flow jumped to ₹851 crore.

How can profit fall 22% while cash flow doubles? It is the working-capital accordion. Because CBFS feedstock and finished carbon black are priced off global crude benchmarks, a drop in crude prices shrinks the rupee value of every barrel of feedstock in storage and every tonne of carbon black invoiced to tire makers. Between March 2025 and March 2026, PCBL's Working Capital Days moved from -24 days to -40 days, turning the balance sheet into a source of cash. Conversely, when crude oil rises or volumes surge—as happened in H1 FY27 when TTM revenue climbed back to ₹8,860 crore—working capital expands again. Indeed, between March 2026 and September 2026, Other Assets rose from ₹3,119 crore to ₹4,229 crore, and borrowings ticked up by ₹94 crore. Treat 85%–100% CFO/EBITDA as PCBL's true through-cycle conversion rate, not 158%.

book_subsections.title: Reading the ₹100 Revenue-to-FCF Waterfall Without Accounting Blind Spots
paragraphs: Walk through our ₹100 revenue waterfall for FY26 with me. Out of every ₹100 of consolidated revenue (₹8,189 Cr total), raw materials and feedstock consume roughly ₹68.50, employee costs take ₹5.80, and other operating expenses absorb ₹13.00—leaving ₹12.74 of operating EBITDA.

Normally, an industrial franchise would keep most of that ₹12.74 after depreciation and tax. At PCBL today, however, depreciation takes ₹4.55 and interest on the Aquapharm debt takes ₹5.17—meaning financial and capital charges consume three-quarters of operating profit before taxes even arrive, leaving just ₹2.42 of net profit per ₹100 of sales. The only reason free cash flow stayed positive at ₹10.39 per ₹100 of sales in FY26 was an extraordinary working-capital release that pushed CFO to ₹19.25 per ₹100 of revenue.

book_callouts.title: The 76% Fixed-Charge Squeeze
book_callouts.text: In FY26, PCBL's ₹796 Cr of combined depreciation (₹373 Cr) and interest (₹423 Cr) consumed 76.3% of its ₹1,043 Cr EBITDA. Until gross debt falls meaningfully or Aquapharm's EBITDA recovers toward ₹300+ Cr/year, small swings in carbon black spreads will cause amplified swings in net profit.
